question.en: Draw a use case diagram for the system described by the following text: An electronic devices vendor has a website where users can search products. When searching, the users first enter the search criteria (type of product, name or brand), and afterwards a list of results is generated and shown to the user. The user can then click on a certain product to see more detailed information, and if he likes it he can add it to the shopping cart. When doing a check-out, the user pays for the content of the shopping cart online. In order to make an online payment, the user has to be logged in. After the payment, the user gets an email message regarding its status.

question.en: Draw a use case diagram for the system described in the following text: The sports center allows users to make reservations for sports halls through a web application. The user can search for available time slots based on selected criteria, such as type of hall (e.g., football, basketball, tennis, etc.) and date. To make a reservation, the user must first log in. After logging in, the user selects a time slot and a hall and makes a reservation. Upon successful reservation, the system automatically sends a confirmation via email. The user can also view their existing reservations and cancel any of them if more than 24 hours remain before the start of the reserved time. Administrators can add new halls, update existing hall information, and manage their availability.

question.en: Draw a use case diagram for the system described in the following text: The library allows registered members to search for and borrow books through a web application. Members can search for books by title, author, or genre. To borrow a book, the member must be logged in. After logging in, the member selects a book, and if there is a copy available a loan is created and the copy is reserved. The user receives a confirmation via email for the successfully borrowed book. Additionally, the user can view which books they currently have borrowed, return books, and submit requests to extend the due date. Librarians can update book data, add new copies, and monitor the status of borrowed books.
